messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — elevated 5xx and request timeouts from gateway (api.redwood.ai). Error rate spiked to 11.9% over the last 3m. Paging oncall.
oncall-juan: ACK. I'm on it. Starting triage — any known deploys in the last 10m?
sre-maya: No deploys from infra in the last 20m. Metrics show scheduler queue depth increasing sharply for model-family 'llama-13b-quant', batch wait times climbing, and gateway 504s. Suspect head-of-line blocking in batch scheduler.
runtime-ryan: Confirming — job queue length on scheduler pods jumped from ~120 to ~4.2k in ~2m. KV cache hit rate unchanged. Looks like some requests are enqueueing very long-running generations that are stalling other batches.
infra-jess: What does the gateway log show? any 502 vs 504 breakdown?
sre-maya: Gateway shows mostly 504/timeouts with upstream connection errors to runtime: "upstream request timed out (110)". Sample logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:20:12Z gateway nginx[pid]: 504 "POST /v1/generate" upstream: "http://runtime-svc:8080" request_time=12.45
2026-03-15T14:21:05Z scheduler[replica-3]: INFO enqueue req_id=0x7f4 long_gen=true seq_len=2048 est_tokens=5000
2026-03-15T14:21:07Z scheduler[replica-3]: WARN batch_wait 450ms queue_len=3800
```
oncall-juan: Ok. Immediate mitigation priorities: 1) reduce impact for time-sensitive customers 2) relieve scheduler queue 3) gather root cause traces. Who can increase scheduler capacity quickly?
runtime-ryan: I can scale scheduler replicas now. scaling helps if the backlog is due to insufficient workers. Running:
```
kubectl scale deploy scheduler -n inference --replicas=6
```
infra-jess: I'm increasing node autoscaler thresholds too in case pods need new nodes.
sre-maya: While we scale, let's also enable emergency throttling at the gateway for non-enterprise routes to protect the rest of the fleet. Proposal: drop requests that look like very long generations (>3k tokens) for free-tier proxies and return 429 with helpful message.
product-amy: Support and product agree — safe throttling for non-SLA traffic ok. Need to coordinate messaging to support teams.
support-leah: I'll draft a short status for affected customers: "We are seeing elevated timeouts and are throttling very long-generation requests to restore service. ETA ~15-30m." Will tag enterprise customers separately if they were impacted.
oncall-juan: Also enable short-term change to scheduler batching: reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 and lower batch timeout from 50ms -> 10ms to reduce head-of-line. runtime-ryan, can you push that config change to all scheduler pods?
runtime-ryan: Pushing now via configmap patch to avoid full rollout:
```
kubectl patch cm scheduler-config -n inference -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"24","batch_wait_ms":"10"}}'
```
runtime-ryan: Patch applied. Confirmed reconcilers updated pods with new env values. Observing reduced batch wait on replica-1 within 30s.
sre-maya: We're seeing queue depth dropping from 4200 -> 1100 over the last 2m. 5xx rate down to ~6.4%.
infra-jess: Node autoscaler added 2 nodes, scheduler replicas are now 6. CPU on GPU nodes trending ok.
runtime-ryan: Added emergency preemption rule: evict any run with est_tokens>8000 from the default queue into a separate low-priority queue to avoid HOL. Applied via runtime feature-flag.
```
rbctl set feature preempt-long-runs=true --env=prod
```
sre-maya: Trace sampling shows a few noisy clients sending many concurrent long sequences — throttling those IPs temporarily. We also routed some traffic to fallback model variant (llama-7b) for non-critical endpoints to reduce run time.
oncall-juan: Good. Can we confirm customer-facing latency for top 10 customers? product-amy / support-leah?
support-leah: Quick snapshot: Top 10 customers — 2 reported errors; we identified one as heavy long-sequence test from internal dev. Notifying affected customers and posting interim status page update.
product-amy: Raising a status note: "Reduced capacity for long-generation requests; most services restored. Engineering continues mitigation." 
oncall-juan: Handing off to SRE for deeper RCA and followup postmortem. @sre-maya take lead. Also create incident ticket and link this thread.
sre-maya: Taking lead. Immediate next steps: capture heap/proc snapshots from scheduler replicas, collect collection of slow-request traces, and review kernel-level socket stats for connection resets. Opening ticket: INC-2026-0487.
runtime-ryan: FYI — found a regression in batching logic where streaming requests with function-calls were not expiring properly from the batch buffer — causes batches to wait indefinitely when a stalled streaming response blocks completion. I'll add a guard to expire streaming-batch entries after 2s if not progressed.
sre-maya: That matches traces. Please create a small patch and roll to one zone as canary.
runtime-ryan: Created PR #6823. Will canary to us-west-2 scheduler replicas in 10m.
product-amy: Support update queued. Also routing note: we used fallback routing to dedicated capacity for a handful of enterprise customers per SLA — no data loss reported.
support-leah: ETA for full mitigation? current 5xx ~2.1% stable after config changes.
oncall-juan: Leave monitoring on for at least 60m. If stable, we'll lift emergency throttles and revert batch settings to pre-incident defaults slowly.
sre-maya: Post-incident action items: 1) add HOL detection alarms (queue depth per priority + per-client), 2) add automatic preempt eviction policy when a request exceeds est token threshold, 3) add a circuit-breaker for streaming function-call flows, 4) add runbook for emergency throttles.
infra-jess: I'll add autoscaler runbook items and a dashboard widget for scheduler backlog per model-family.
product-amy: I'll coordinate customer comms and ensure enterprise SLAs are checked; also flag compensation if any paying customer saw degraded SLA.
oncall-juan: Thanks all. I'll stay on the thread for 30m to verify stability. Please drop final notes here and tag INC-2026-0487 once postmortem skeleton is created.
sre-maya: Final note: mitigation actions (scale up, reduce batch size, preempt long runs, throttle non-SLA) restored service. Root cause suspected batching regression + a short burst of long-running sequences. Postmortem in progress.
support-leah: Status sent to impacted customers and support queue updated. Closing paging loop. :white_check_mark:
